citation: Partridge BL. The effects of local anesthetics and epinephrine on rat sciatic nerve blood flow. Anesthesiology 1991;75(2):243-50
what_it_shows: Wiesmann reference 8. Randomised, blinded rat experiment (45 rats, 90 sciatic nerves, laser Doppler): topical epinephrine at three concentrations, the lowest being the one C074 names, alone and with lidocaine, plus bupivacaine and tetracaine. At the lowest concentration epinephrine alone briefly raised nerve blood flow; the two higher ones reduced it; combined with lidocaine every pairing reduced flow synergistically. It remains the only nerve blood-flow measurement at C074's concentration.
quote_from_abstract: Sciatic NBF was measured by laser doppler in 45 adult female Sprague-Dawley rats (90 nerves) after topical application of [dose figure omitted] lidocaine and epinephrine, alone and in combination (lidocaine plus epinephrine), as well as bupivacaine, tetracaine, and normal saline, and studied in a randomized, blinded experimental design.

citation: Myers RR, Heckman HM. Effects of local anesthesia on nerve blood flow: studies using lidocaine with and without epinephrine. Anesthesiology 1989;71(5):757-62
what_it_shows: Wiesmann reference 4. Rat sciatic nerve blood flow by laser Doppler over 10 min after topical saline, lidocaine with and without epinephrine, or epinephrine alone, at an epinephrine concentration higher than C074's. Every solution except saline reduced flow; epinephrine added to lidocaine reduced flow more than lidocaine alone.
quote_from_abstract: Epinephrine by itself significantly reduced nerve blood flow; when added to local anesthetic solutions, it reduced nerve blood flow to a greater extent than the reduction caused by anesthetics alone.

citation: Palmer GM, Cairns BE, Berkes SL, Dunning PS, Taylor GA, Berde CB. The effects of lidocaine and adrenergic agonists on rat sciatic nerve and skeletal muscle blood flow in vivo. Anesth Analg 2002;95(4):1080-6
what_it_shows: Wiesmann reference 22. Rat sciatic nerve and muscle blood flow by radiolabelled microspheres after perisciatic injection of lidocaine, epinephrine (the same concentration Wiesmann used, higher than C074's and higher than Myers's), phenylephrine, or combinations. Lidocaine alone and epinephrine alone did not alter nerve or muscle flow; lidocaine with epinephrine mildly reduced nerve flow at 30 min. Not a measurement at C074's concentration.
quote_from_abstract: Lidocaine ([dose figure omitted]) and epinephrine ([dose figure omitted]) injected alone did not alter blood flow in sciatic nerve, perisciatic muscle, or masseter muscle.

citation: Bouaziz H, Iohom G, Estèbe JP, Campana WM, Myers RR. Effects of levobupivacaine and ropivacaine on rat sciatic nerve blood flow. Br J Anaesth 2005;95(5):696-700
what_it_shows: Wiesmann reference 9. 48 rats; laser Doppler nerve blood flow for 30 min after topical saline, lidocaine, levobupivacaine, ropivacaine, or ropivacaine with epinephrine (a concentration higher than C074's), and histology at 48 h. All local anaesthetics reduced nerve blood flow; adding epinephrine did not reduce it further than ropivacaine alone; no significant histological change at 48 h. A further nerve blood-flow measurement with epinephrine that C074's records did not list, not at C074's concentration.
quote_from_abstract: The combination of ropivacaine [dose figure omitted] plus epinephrine did not reduce nerve blood flow to a greater extent than ropivacaine [dose figure omitted] alone.

citation: Choi CH, Pak SC, Jang CH. Effect of local anesthesia on facial nerve blood flow and muscle action potential. Int J Pediatr Otorhinolaryngol 2016;82:43-6
what_it_shows: Found by a PubMed search on nerve blood flow and epinephrine run for this paper (not in Wiesmann's reference list). Rat facial nerve, gelfoam soaked in lidocaine with or without epinephrine laid on the nerve for 30 min (n = 5 per group): facial nerve blood flow fell, more with epinephrine than with lidocaine alone, and conduction threshold rose then recovered. Epinephrine concentration higher than C074's, so not a second measurement at that concentration.
quote_from_abstract: Synergistic reduction in FNBF was greater in groups A and B than in the lidocaine applied groups (C and D).

citation: Ibrahim S, Laude EA, Bee D, Eaton S, Ward JD, Harris ND. Combined microlightguide spectrophotometry and microendoscopy for measurement of oxygen saturation in peripheral nerves. Physiol Meas 1999;20(1):65-73
what_it_shows: Wiesmann reference 29. Measured nerve oxygen saturation and nerve perfusion together in the sciatic nerves of 12 healthy rats (no drug applied); nerve saturation fell with systemic hypoxia. Bears on the Lidocaine With Epinephrine Wheals page's description of Wiesmann as 'the one study that measured flow and oxygen on the same nerve' (true only for studies with a local anaesthetic). No tested claim.
quote_from_abstract: We have used a combination of microlightguide spectrophotometry and microendoscopy to measure intravascular oxygen saturation (HbSaO2%) and monitor blood flow in the sciatic nerve of 12 healthy male Sprague-Dawley rats.

citation: Shishido H, Kikuchi S, Heckman H, Myers RR. Dexamethasone decreases blood flow in normal nerves and dorsal root ganglia. Spine 2002;27(6):581-6
what_it_shows: Found by a PubMed search on adjuvants and nerve blood flow run for this paper (not in Wiesmann's reference list). Rat sciatic nerve, laser Doppler: topical dexamethasone significantly reduced nerve blood flow at 30 min and 4 h (some animals first showed a brief rise), with only minimal oedema on histology at 2-6 days. Evidence that dexamethasone acts on nerve vessels, against the adjuvants page's 'no action on a blood vessel at all'.
quote_from_abstract: Dexamethasone causes statistically significant reductions in normal nerve blood flow at 30 minutes and 4 hours after topical application; however, the reduction is on average below the threshold for causing ischemic changes in the structure of peripheral nerve fibers.

citation: Fukusaki M, Miyako M, Nakamura T, Miyoshi H, Sumikawa K, Konishi H, Hara S. Perineural injection to nerve root and radicular blood flow: a clinical study during spinal surgery. Eur J Anaesthesiol 2001;18(2):70-4
what_it_shows: Found by the same search (not in Wiesmann's reference list). Randomised trial in 30 patients during lumbar discectomy: laser Doppler on the exposed nerve root before and 15 min after perineural saline, lidocaine or dexamethasone; radicular blood flow did not change in any group. The one human nerve-root flow measurement after dexamethasone: no short-term change, unlike rat sciatic nerve (Shishido 2002).
quote_from_abstract: The results suggest that the perineural injection of [dose figure omitted] lidocaine or dexamethasone does not affect radicular blood flow during lumbar discectomy.

citation: Andersen P, Milioni K, Maibach H. The cutaneous corticosteroid vasoconstriction assay: a reflectance spectroscopic and laser-Doppler flowmetric study. Br J Dermatol 1993;128(6):660-5
what_it_shows: Found by a PubMed search on dexamethasone and skin vasoconstriction run for this paper (not in Wiesmann's reference list). Human skin, topical corticosteroids under occlusion, visual scoring, reflectance spectroscopy and laser Doppler: dexamethasone caused significant visible blanching, mainly venoconstriction (fall in deoxygenated haemoglobin) without a significant fall in laser-Doppler flow. Direct human evidence that dexamethasone acts on skin vessels.
quote_from_abstract: Fluocinolone acetonide, betamethasone-17-valerate and dexamethasone also caused visible blanching (P < 0.01).

citation: Anderson CR, Morris RL, Boeh SD, Panus PC, Sembrowich WL. Effects of iontophoresis current magnitude and duration on dexamethasone deposition and localized drug retention. Phys Ther 2003;83(2):161-70
what_it_shows: Found by the same search (not in Wiesmann's reference list). Dexamethasone driven into human skin by iontophoresis in volunteers produced visible cutaneous vasoconstriction, used by the authors as the sign that the drug had reached the vessels. A second human observation of dexamethasone constricting skin vessels.
quote_from_abstract: Delivery of DEX/DEX-P to at least the depths of the vasculature in humans was confirmed by observation of cutaneous vasoconstriction.
